resolution_boundary.next_step: A later resolution proposal must identify declaration IDs and bind new evidence; this view is not a completed resolution ledger.

open_blockers.claim: The stop arm reaches the rest of the button only through a sliver overlap with the barrel, and no check covers this load path. The arm box (x -14..-12, y 15..23.5, z 9.8..13.4) shares only 0.663 mm3 with the barrel cylinder (r 2.4, z>=13). That is a 1.66 mm2 footprint, 0.4 mm tall, sitting on the z=13 plane, which is a layer interface in the stated print orientation (bore vertical). The arm's own section is 7.2 mm2 at y=22. Every rest-preload and hard-stop reaction passes through this joint. The stop face is 10 mm from the hinge, while thumb load at the far face edge acts about 27 mm from it, so the joint load is up to about 2.7x the thumb force. If the joint fails, both the rest stop (F2) and the overtravel stop (F5) are lost at once. Revision 1 was faulted for the same class of defect (MFG-TONGUE-ROOT, a 0.5x1.0 mm strip). The round-2 review required a connectivity and minimum-section check, and revision 2 carries neither.
evidence: Independent CadQuery 2.8 on button/model.step: arm∩barrel volume 0.6629 mm3, footprint 1.657 mm2 (z 13.0..13.4)
Horizontal slice of the button in the arm footprint at z=12.99: 17.0 mm2 (arm only). At z=13.01: 17.69 mm2 (arm plus 0.69 mm2 of barrel). The barrel starts at z=13.
Vertical slice at y=22.0: 7.2 mm2, z 9.8..13.4 (arm alone, not joined to the barrel)
side_button_recipe.py stop_arm box y_max = hinge_y - barrel_inner_radius - 0.4 = 23.5. barrel_z_min 13.0. stop_arm_z_max 13.4.
design_basis: 'button printed with the bore vertical' (layers parallel to the z=13 joint)
No wall_check, section or connectivity check names the stop arm. button-printed-wall samples only 10 points per face (min 1.30 mm).
open_blockers.proposed_change: Root the stop arm into the barrel over its full height. For example, start the barrel at the arm's z_min, or extend the arm up the barrel side with a gusset to the link, so the stop reaction does not cross a single 0.4 mm layer band. State a minimum root section.
open_blockers.required_test: Add a section check: the minimum cross-section of the button between the stop-arm contact face (x=-14 / x=-12 faces at y 15..18.5) and the barrel bore must be >= a stated value (for example >= the 7.2 mm2 arm section), with no single horizontal plane carrying less than that value. Negative control: the current geometry must fail it (1.66 mm2).

open_blockers.claim: The stop arm, which carries both the rest stop (F2) and the hard overtravel stop (F5), joins the button only through a tiny layer-line joint. The arm (x -14..-12, y 15..23.5, z 9.8..13.4) is a separate island below the barrel: a section at z 12.95 has 2 solids, and the arm joins at z 13.0. The joint is the horizontal arm-on-barrel overlap of 1.657 mm2 (z 13.0-13.4), plus a curved side patch of roughly 0.8 mm2. The arm's own section is 7.2 mm2. The declared orientation prints the bore vertical, which makes this joint an interlayer bond whichever end is down. The stop contact is the arm corner at y about 15, z 9.8-12, roughly 8 mm along y and 2 mm down from the joint. The x-direction stop reaction therefore twists and peels that layer joint. The arm sits at radius 10 mm and the face centre at lever 15 mm, so the arm reaction is about 1.5x the thumb force at the face centre and up to 2.7x at the far end of the face. A simple rectangular-section torsion estimate gives tens of MPa of interlayer shear per newton of arm force. On that estimate the hard stop would shear off on ordinary presses. After that, nothing designed limits overtravel into the switch.
evidence: Recipe v2 stop_arm box z 9.8..13.4 versus barrel_outer z 13.0..17.5; link_box starts at x -11.1 and does not reach the arm (x <= -12).
My CadQuery section of button/model.step: z=12.95 gives 2 solids (the arm is an island); z=13.05 gives 1 solid.
Area of arm footprint intersected with the barrel annulus at z=13: 1.657 mm2. Vertical section of the arm at y 16-22.5: 7.2 mm2.
Recipe design_basis: 'button printed with the bore vertical', so the joint plane z=13 is a layer plane.
Rotation checks rest-outward-blocked and hard-stop-blocks-past-stop both depend on this arm; no check measures its root section or strength.
The r1 and r2 manufacturing reviews raised the same failure mode (MFG-TONGUE-ROOT, root about 3.75 mm2). Revision 2 moved the stop to a new arm whose root is smaller still.
open_blockers.proposed_change: Join the stop arm to the barrel along a vertical interface over the full barrel height. For example, extend stop_arm z_max to the barrel top (17.5, or the common top plane if the button top faces are levelled, see MFG-BUTTON-ORIENT). The arm then sits in the barrel's layers rather than hanging under it. Keep y_max at 23.5 so the 0.4 mm bore wall stays intact, and check against tab_high (bottom 17.7, y >= 22). Alternatively add a gusset from the arm's top face to the barrel side up to z 17.5. Do not reduce the arm or stop loads to pass.
open_blockers.required_test: Re-section the revised button: the arm region must be connected at every z with no island, and the minimal cut between arm and barrel must be at least the arm's own 7.2 mm2 section, mostly on vertical planes in the declared orientation. Re-run all rotation, motion and wall checks unchanged. Physical test: print the button in the declared orientation and material, mount it on the pin in a printed shell, and load the stop arm through repeated full presses plus a stated overload at the face end. Record the failure load and mode.

open_blockers.claim: The rest stop (arm on block_out) and the hard stop (arm on block_in) both act on a stop arm only 1.5-10 mm from the pivot. The plunger sits about 15 mm out and the face about 27 mm out. Any bodily shift of the button inside its radial play therefore moves both stop angles by roughly +/-0.12/10 rad (about +/-0.6 deg), and that error is amplified at the plunger and at the face. The verification plan states 'Housing stays clear until the stop angle at every hinge-play offset'. housing-clear-until-stop sweeps every play offset only to the NOMINAL stop angle (-3.438 deg), not to the stop angle that the offset button actually reaches, so the check passes while the stated contract fails. Inside the declared 0.1 mm play I measured a counterexample on the exported STEP: housing clearance of 0.118 mm at the real stop, below the recipe's own 0.2 mm requirement. The same offsets also consume the 0.2 mm rest free play, leave the stem pre-pressed at rest, and let the face rest outward of flush on the opposite side. The datum that should hold the flush rest pose and the overtravel limit is not where the controlled features are.
evidence: Exported STEP, read-only CadQuery 2.8 probe: button rotated about (-13,25) and translated by an in-plane offset. Stop angle found by bisection on overlap > 1e-6 mm3 with the shell near the hinge. Stem displacement = translation of switch_stem in -Y until no overlap.
Nominal (offset 0): stop -3.449 deg at block_in (-14.60, 15.08, 9.80); stem displacement 0.766 mm; housing clearance 0.309 mm; rest 0 deg; rest stem gap 0.200 mm.

Offset (+0.092, -0.038) mm, radius 0.1 = declared hinge_radial_play_mm: stop -3.983 deg; stem displacement 0.948 mm; housing clearance 0.118 mm (< 0.2 required); rest angle -0.819 deg with the plunger already overlapping the stem (rest gap 0, overlap 0.206 mm3).
Offset (+0.100, 0): stop -4.028 deg; housing 0.144 mm; rest -0.881 deg with the stem pre-pressed.

Offset (-0.100, 0): stop -2.872 deg; stem displacement 0.609 mm; rest +0.574 deg, i.e. rotated outward. A 2D point model of the same geometry puts the far face edge point (14, 29.03) about 0.27 mm outward of its drawn position.

The model has 0.02 mm more radial play that the checks do not count: tab_hole_radius 1.02 vs pin 1.00, overlap-shell-hinge_pin distance 0.020 mm. At radius 0.12, offset (+0.111, -0.046) gives a stop of -4.090 deg, stem displacement 0.985 mm and housing clearance 0.080 mm. Offset (-0.111, +0.046) gives a stop of -2.810 deg and stem displacement 0.546 mm, only 0.046 mm above the 0.5 mm assumed operating travel.
measurements.json housing-clear-until-stop: axis_play_mm 0.1, every offset swept with end_deg -3.4377 only; continuous lower bound 0.185 mm < min 0.2, 'not_proven', verdict pass.
measurements.json rest-outward-blocked, shell-clear-until-stop and hard-stop-blocks-past-stop all ran with axis_play_mm 0.0, so play is never applied to the stop or rest features themselves.
open_blockers.proposed_change: Locate rest and overtravel at a radius at least as large as the plunger's, so that hinge play is not amplified. Examples: put the stop pair on the plunger or rib near x 0..3 against shell-fixed faces, or put the hard stop on the face/rib against the switch carrier. Or reduce the effective radial play, including the tab-hole play, until the swept envelope meets the 0.2 mm housing margin and the 0.2 mm rest free play. Count tab-hole play in hinge_radial_play_mm, or declare it separately. Whatever the fix, the stated contract must not claim housing clearance 'at every hinge-play offset' until the check measures it.
open_blockers.required_test: For each of at least 16 radial offsets at the full radial play (bore play plus tab-hole play), find the actual hard-stop angle by bisection against the shell and evaluate at that angle: housing clearance >= 0.2 mm, and stem displacement >= assumed operating travel + margin. At the same offsets, find the outward rest angle and assert that the plunger-to-stem gap stays >= 0 (ideally the declared free play) and that the face does not sit outward of the skin by more than an owner-set flush tolerance. Run rest-outward-blocked and hard-stop-blocks-past-stop with axis_play_mm > 0.
